lessons.title: Triton kernel: dynamic-bound loops must not use Python range()
lessons.symptom: Review flagged vllm_ascend/ops/triton/mamba/postprocess.py: `for i in range(0, copy_size, COPY_BLOCK_SIZE)` where copy_size is a runtime value — Triton evaluates range() at compile time and requires constexpr bounds, so compilation fails (or silently miscompiles) once the copy path runs.
lessons.root_cause: The Triton kernel copy loop was written with Python range() semantics; Triton only allows compile-time-constant bounds there.  Runtime bounds need a `while` loop (Triton 2.x+) or tl.static_range with a constexpr cap + runtime mask.
fix_guidance: In any Triton kernel, check every loop bound: if it is loaded from a pointer, derived from runtime tensors, or passed as a non-constexpr arg, it is NOT valid for range()
Use `while i < copy_size:` with `i += BLOCK` or `tl.static_range(MAX_ITERS)` + `if i < num_iters:` mask
After syncing a kernel from upstream, grep for `range(` with non-constexpr bounds before merging
lessons.example: gemini code review on PR #13823 flagged mamba/postprocess.py:166; the upstream vllm kernel this was synced from uses the same loop shape, so verify against upstream's while-loop pattern.

lessons.title: E2E model/LoRA adapter download failures are environment, not adaptation
lessons.symptom: test_qwen3_multi_loras failed all 3 e2e rounds with `Exception: Call to add_lora method failed: Loading lora Alice failed: No adapter found for charent/self_cognition_Alice` — the LoRA adapter model is missing from the runner cache and cannot be downloaded.
lessons.root_cause: The e2e case needs a model/LoRA adapter that is not pre-cached on the runner; download fails (offline/cache miss).  This is an environment gap, not an adaptation defect — 3 fix rounds were wasted on it and the whole run was discarded.
fix_guidance: Before treating an e2e failure as an adaptation bug, check whether the error is a model download / adapter-not-found / HF offline message — that is an env issue, skip the case or pre-cache the model
A single environment-dependent case failing 3 rounds discards the whole run (no commit, no PR) — classify env failures early
lessons.example: run 31262305861: multi_loras failed rounds 0-2 with adapter-not-found; npu_ipc_weight_transfer failed alongside.

lessons.title: npu_ipc_weight_transfer e2e fails persistently (needs investigation)
lessons.symptom: test_npu_ipc_weight_transfer_updates_server_weights failed all 3 e2e rounds of run 31262305861 even after the adapter fixed npu_ipc_engine.py and the test file — the server-side weight update path raises at runtime.
lessons.root_cause: Not yet diagnosed: either a real adaptation gap in the trainer weight-transfer runtime path or an environment issue (server startup/connection).  The failure is persistent across rounds, so it is likely real — needs a targeted traceback review before the case can be trusted as a per-step signal.
fix_guidance: When a case fails 3 consecutive rounds with the same test, read the round-N traceback directly (it is in the workspace artifact) rather than re-adapting blind
Persistent failures that are not model-download env issues are the highest-value fix targets
lessons.example: run 31262305861 rounds 0-2; the case was removed from the per-step allowlist (test_policy.json) as a stopgap.

lessons.title: Version-guarded conditional logic: nested guards + init-state checks
lessons.symptom: Human review (PR #13477) found model_runner_v1.py's routed_experts clear_buffer change incorrect: the version-guarded nested conditions (vllm_version_is('0.26.0') AND enable_return_routed_experts AND routed_experts_initialized) were flattened/wrong, changing behavior on the release branch.
lessons.root_cause: When adapting a version-dependent code path, the reviewer pattern is: the vllm_version_is guard must wrap the ENTIRE release-specific behavior, and each nested condition (feature flag, init state) must be preserved — flattening or reordering them changes which branch runs on 0.26.0 vs main.
fix_guidance: For any version-dependent block, write the guard as `if vllm_version_is('0.26.0'):` wrapping ALL release behavior, preserving every nested flag/state check
When removing or modifying a guarded block, diff against BOTH versions — the release branch keeps the old behavior
Before merging, check the patch file description list (vllm_ascend/patch/__init__.py) is updated when a patch changes
For Triton kernel changes, get model-owner confirmation (performance regression check) — review standard on PR #13477
lessons.example: PR #13477 model_runner_v1.py review: 'This change is incorrect, it should be: if vllm_version_is(0.26.0): if enable_return_routed_experts: if routed_experts_initialized: clear_buffer()'

lessons.title: Test patches a vllm constant that moved modules — update the patch target
lessons.symptom: CPU-UT setup error: `AttributeError: <module 'vllm.v1.spec_decode.extract_hidden_states'> does not have the attribute 'PIN_MEMORY'` in tests/ut/spec_decode/test_extract_hidden_states_proposer.py — the fixture patches the old module location.
lessons.root_cause: vllm moved PIN_MEMORY from vllm.v1.spec_decode.extract_hidden_states to vllm.utils.torch_utils; the old module now only IMPORTS it (does not define it), so patch('vllm.v1.spec_decode.extract_hidden_states.PIN_MEMORY') fails at setup with create=False.
fix_guidance: When a patch('vllm.X.Y.Z', ...) fails with 'does not have the attribute', find where vllm actually defines the symbol now (`grep -rn SYMBOL vllm/`) and patch the NEW location
A module that merely imports a name does not expose it for patching — patch the DEFINING module
lessons.example: Fix: patch 'vllm.utils.torch_utils.PIN_MEMORY' instead of 'vllm.v1.spec_decode.extract_hidden_states.PIN_MEMORY'.  PR #13879 CI failure.

lessons.title: Test mocks a vllm torch op that upstream removed — drop the mock
lessons.symptom: CPU-UT setup error: `AttributeError: 'torch.ops.vllm' does not have the attribute 'maybe_calc_kv_scales'` in tests/ut/spec_decode/test_speculators_vwn_eagle3.py:_mock_npu_env at line 148.
lessons.root_cause: Upstream [dd11df04] 'Remove deprecated calculate_kv_scales' deleted the op registration; the test still patches torch.ops.vllm.maybe_calc_kv_scales.  The SAME fix was applied in a previous main2main PR (#13823) but the adapter did not re-apply it when re-adapting from a fresh baseline.
fix_guidance: When torch.ops.vllm.X is missing, the op was removed upstream — delete the patch.object(torch.ops.vllm, 'X', ...) line (and any source use)
For test files, check the PREVIOUS main2main PRs' diffs for the same test — fixes applied before must be re-applied on every fresh baseline run
After adapting source, grep tests/ut for the removed/renamed vllm symbol and sync the test files too — source adaptation alone leaves the CPU-UT gate red
lessons.example: PR #13879: test_speculators_vwn_eagle3.py:148 still patches maybe_calc_kv_scales; the fix is to remove that line (as PR #13823 did).
